audit.whatIsWrong: Both item stages were given to Gnar while whys[5], whys[6], spikes[2] and the late-game text all argue Karma reclaims and keeps the lane from her first item onward.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is Skill, Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Karma, Karma, and the gnar__karma audit explicitly left the instruction to restate the item stages as Karma's. Emerald+ win rate is 64.29%, which is a Karma-favoured lane once her items land.
audit.corrected: Rows 5 and 6 -> Karma in both layers as one atomic pair group, with both phase whys rewritten so the reason matches the new side. Rows 0-4 already agreed with the mirror.

audit.why: The page already states that level 6 gives Karma nothing because Mantra is usable from level 1, and correctly frames Gnar's spike as Rage-driven rather than level-driven. spikes[] keeps its 4 entries with the item spike named.
audit.corrected: No change needed beyond naming the boomerang range in the first-item phase.
sources: kit: Karma R 'available at level 1 and does not require a skill point'

audit.whatIsWrong: The core range claim ('out-range my Inner Flame') was asserted with no numbers, 'Soulflare' was used as the name of the Mantra-empowered Q, and the Hop-breaks-tether line never said what actually breaks it.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw is 1100 range against Inner Flame's 950 — the range gap is real and is the whole reason levels 2-3 are his. Focused Resolve is broken by leaving 675 range, which is exactly what Hop (22/19.5/17/14.5/12s, 475) does. Riot's text names no Soulflare; the Mantra Q bonus is a cataclysm.
audit.corrected: 1100-vs-950 written into whys[0], whys[1] and the first-item phase; the 675 break distance and Hop's 22s rank-1 timer written into wants.foe[2] and the do's; Soulflare replaced with Mantra-Q in the fields edited.
sources: kit: Karma Q range 950, W range 675
